title: The hazelnut
hookLine: Julian of Norwich sees all that is made as small as a hazelnut in her palm, lasting because it is loved (Revelations of Divine Love 5)

cards: There's a photo of Earth taken from far out in space: a tiny pale dot, almost lost in a beam of light. Everything is on there. Everyone who ever lived.

Every war, every wedding, every lunch. And it's so small. Long before any camera left the planet, a woman in England, very sick and close to death, saw something like that, except it was sitting in the palm of her hand.

teach.b: In May of 1373, a woman in Norwich, in England, was thirty and a half years old and so ill that everyone expected her to die. A priest held a crucifix in front of her eyes.
Over the next hours she received what she called sixteen showings, visions about the love of God. She recovered, and wrote the showings down.
By her own account, she was still being taught what one of them meant close to twenty years later. The book is called Revelations of Divine Love. Her own name isn't known for certain.
Tradition says she lived as an anchoress, in a small room attached to the church of Saint Julian in Norwich, and she's remembered as Julian after that church.
Early in the book, she says she was shown a little thing, the size of a hazelnut, lying in the palm of her hand, round as a ball. She looked at it and wondered what it could be.

The answer came, in Grace Warrack's old translation: "It is all that is made." The whole created world, in one palm. She marveled how it could last; it seemed so small it might just fall into nothing.
And she understood: it lasts, and always will, because God loves it.
She saw three things in that little ball: God made it, God loves it, God keeps it. Christians who read Julian often come back to this picture. For anyone, it's a way of looking at small things.
A stone, a cup, a hand. Small enough to fall into nothing. Still here.

how: Christians of many churches read Julian of Norwich's Revelations of Divine Love as a classic of prayer, and some church calendars, Anglican ones among them, remember her in May.

o: Julian's vision of all creation, small in her palm
a nut she ate to break a long fast in her cell
a token pilgrims carried home from Norwich

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.
p: lived in a room beside a church

s: not for certain. tradition links the name Julian to the church she lived beside.
she was told the little thing lasts because God loves it
it lasts, and ever shall, she writes, for God loves it.
the hazelnut was a real nut she was holding
it was a showing: a little thing that seemed to lie in her palm, and the answer was: all that is made.

games.q: you're Julian. in your palm is a little thing, round as a ball, the size of a hazelnut. you ask what it is. what's the answer?
o: a seed of the tree of life
games.why: it is all that is made. and it lasts, she understands, because God loves it: God made it, God loves it, God keeps it.

practice: Pick up something small near you, a coin, a button, a pebble, a nut, a ring, or if there's nothing, look at your own open palm.
Look at it longer than feels normal: its color, its edges, its weight, how easily it could be lost, and that it's here anyway. If you pray, you can hold Julian's three words: made, loved, kept.

wordCard.voice: The hazelnut. Julian's vision of everything that is made, small enough to sit in her palm, lasting because it is loved.

carryVoice: Your line: all that is made. Small as it is, it lasts. See you at day eighty-nine.
